summary.notes: All 75 items PASS D4 (authoritative standards correctly cited, zero fabricated citations). All 75 items PASS D5 on the specific criteria checked (prompts reference company name, calculation inputs traceable, no ambiguous wording, no conflicting data). However, all 15 cases share a critical structural limitation: zero exhibits (ExhibitCount=0), identically templated ScenarioText (CMA-style review meeting framing), no named stakeholder role, and no business trigger event. Every item is answerable as a standalone MCQ without the case context. The 'case' wrapper provides cosmetic company-name threading but no integrated case experience. This is flagged as a design-level concern rather than a per-item D5 failure under the stated criteria.

design_concerns.description: All 15 cases share a common structural limitation: zero exhibits, identical templated ScenarioText ('CMA-style review meeting'), no named stakeholder with a specific role, and no business trigger event. All 75 items reference the company name in their prompts but are answerable as standalone MCQs without the case context. The 'case' wrapper provides cosmetic company-name threading (each case groups 5 same-section MCQs under one fictional company) but does not create an integrated case-study experience. This is a design-level observation, not a per-item D4/D5 failure under the stated criteria — all items pass the specific checks required (company referenced, no fabricated citations, calculation inputs traceable, no ambiguous wording, no conflicting data).
design_concerns.recommendation: For the cases to meet CAQS case-study standards (CAQS v1.0 §3), each case would need: named stakeholder with decision-making role, a business trigger event, exhibits that items depend on (at minimum 2 per case per QUESTION_METADATA_STANDARD.md §1.1), and items that use exhibit data rather than carrying all values in the prompt itself.

standards_citation_audit.notes: All 41 explicit standard citations across 75 items are real, correctly attributed, and topically relevant. Conceptual/managerial-accounting items (budgeting, standard costing, process costing, etc.) appropriately do not cite specific ASC/IFRS/IAS standards since those topics fall under managerial accounting principles rather than GAAP/IFRS reporting standards.
